3.19.9 Expulsion and Re-Admission
1.A student shall be expelled from the program and not allowed to return to the same program in
any of the following cases:
a. If he/she fails in any course twice.
b. If he/she fails in three courses in the study throughout his/her entire time in the program.
c. If he/she fails the comprehensive examination twice.
d. If he/she commits a violation that is punishable by expulsion in accordance with the university
by-laws and regulations.
e. If he/she received two” no-pass” in the thesis defense.

f. If he/she fails in any of the remedial courses.
2. The dismissed student may be allowed to return to the same program, except for the provision
of Article 17, in the following cases:
a. If he/she withdraws from all courses in the first semester of his/her studies (subject to the
provisions of Article 34 of these regulations).
b. If he/she does not receive the minimum cumulative average (3 out of 4) at the third warning
(subject to the provisions of Article 35 of these regulations).
A student expelled from a program may not return to the same program but may apply for another program in accordance with the conditions of the new program. A maximum of 12 relevant credit hours may be transferred to the new program provided that a maximum of 4 years elapsed since he/she finished the transferred courses.
The previous statement  shall not be applied to a student expelled from a program due to a fall in his/her CGPA. He/she may register for a maximum of 9 credit hours for the purpose of raising his/her CGPA as a “special study student”. He/she may re-register in his/her original program once his/her CGPA becomes 3 again provided the following:
a. His/her CGPA at the time of expulsion was not less than 2.5 out of 4. b. The student may be placed under a “special study” status for a maximum period of two semesters,
and this period shall not count as part of the time limit set for graduation.

3.19.11 Attendance
If a student’s absence exceeds 25% of the total number of teaching hours in the courses that demand attendance without an excuse acceptable to the instructor and approved by the Dean, the student shall be barred from the final examination and will receive a grade of “F”. He/she may also duly withdraw from the course if the drop period still applies in accordance with the regulations. If a student’s absence reaches more than 25% of the total number of teaching hours in the courses that demand attendance with a medical excuse or an excuse which is acceptable to the instructor and approved by the Dean, the student shall be deemed to have withdrawn from the course, and the grade “W” (withdrawn) shall be entered in his/her record.
94
3.19.12 Registration of Thesis
Theses shall be written either in Arabic or English in accordance with the Deanship guidelines and the Department requirements provided that an abstract is written in the other language. A supervisor and a joint supervisor (if needed) shall be appointed for the thesis from among the Department faculty, giving consideration to the student’s selection as much as possible, by a decision of the Dean and upon a recommendation from the Graduate Studies Committee in the Department.
University theses shall be supervised by professors and associate professors. An assistant professor may also supervise a thesis provided that he/she has been teaching at the university level for a minimum of two years and has at least two papers in his field of specialization published or accepted for publication in journals recognized by the university. Faculty or qualified professionals from outside the Department may act as joint supervisors (co-supervisors) by a decision of the Council.
Application to supervise a thesis proposal must include an updated resume of the supervisor who is undertaking supervision for the first time. The supervisor is expected to have at least two papers published or accepted for publication over the past five years in refereed journals recognized by the university.
The maximum number of theses a supervisor may supervise at any one time will be as follows:
• Professor: 5 theses
• Associate professor: 4 theses
• Assistant professor: 3 theses The Dean may increase the number of theses for each supervisor in accordance with the legitimate needs of the Department and with the approval of the Graduate Studies Committee in the Department.
The supervisor may be changed in justifiable circumstances, and with the same conditions for the appointment of a supervisor.
A faculty member on sabbatical leave or unpaid leave may, by a decision of the Council and upon the recommendation of the Department, continue to supervise a student’s thesis or participate in the supervision thereof if he/she is spending the leave within the United Arab Emirates.
A student may register the thesis after the completion of 50% of total credit hours, and after completing all the remedial courses and any other conditions stipulated for admission, including the English language requirements. The students should also maintain a CPGA of 3 out of 4.
The following steps must be followed in the approval of the thesis proposal:
a. The student will submit an application along with the thesis proposal on a special form prepared
by the Deanship to the chairman of the Department in accordance with the proposal guidelines
the Deanship prepares.
b. The chairman of the Department / the program coordinator will set a public date for the discussion
of the proposal which will be attended by the supervisor, the faculty members in the Department,
and the postgraduate students within two weeks from the date of submission.

3.19.11 Attendance
If a student’s absence exceeds 25% of the total number of teaching hours in the courses that demand attendance without an excuse acceptable to the instructor and approved by the Dean, the student shall be barred from the final examination and will receive a grade of “F”. He/she may also duly withdraw from the course if the drop period still applies in accordance with the regulations. If a student’s absence reaches more than 25% of the total number of teaching hours in the courses that demand attendance with a medical excuse or an excuse which is acceptable to the instructor and approved by the Dean, the student shall be deemed to have withdrawn from the course, and the grade “W” (withdrawn) shall be entered in his/her record.

3.19.12 Registration of Thesis
Theses shall be written either in Arabic or English in accordance with the Deanship guidelines and the Department requirements provided that an abstract is written in the other language. A supervisor and a joint supervisor (if needed) shall be appointed for the thesis from among the Department faculty, giving consideration to the student’s selection as much as possible, by a decision of the Dean and upon a recommendation from the Graduate Studies Committee in the Department.
University theses shall be supervised by professors and associate professors. An assistant professor may also supervise a thesis provided that he/she has been teaching at the university level for a minimum of two years and has at least two papers in his field of specialization published or accepted for publication in journals recognized by the university. Faculty or qualified professionals from outside the Department may act as joint supervisors (co-supervisors) by a decision of the Council.
Application to supervise a thesis proposal must include an updated resume of the supervisor who is undertaking supervision for the first time. The supervisor is expected to have at least two papers published or accepted for publication over the past five years in refereed journals recognized by the university.
The maximum number of theses a supervisor may supervise at any one time will be as follows:
• Professor: 5 theses
• Associate professor: 4 theses
• Assistant professor: 3 theses The Dean may increase the number of theses for each supervisor in accordance with the legitimate needs of the Department and with the approval of the Graduate Studies Committee in the Department.
The supervisor may be changed in justifiable circumstances, and with the same conditions for the appointment of a supervisor.
A faculty member on sabbatical leave or unpaid leave may, by a decision of the Council and upon the recommendation of the Department, continue to supervise a student’s thesis or participate in the supervision thereof if he/she is spending the leave within the United Arab Emirates.
A student may register the thesis after the completion of 50% of total credit hours, and after completing all the remedial courses and any other conditions stipulated for admission, including the English language requirements. The students should also maintain a CPGA of 3 out of 4.
The following steps must be followed in the approval of the thesis proposal:
a. The student will submit an application along with the thesis proposal on a special form prepared
by the Deanship to the chairman of the Department in accordance with the proposal guidelines
the Deanship prepares.
b. The chairman of the Department / the program coordinator will set a public date for the discussion
of the proposal which will be attended by the supervisor, the faculty members in the Department,
and the postgraduate students within two weeks from the date of submission.

a. The number of the committee members will be at least three (apart from the main supervisor

c. One of the committee members, who is qualified and competent to carry out this task, maybe a

3.19.14 Procedures for Thesis Discussion
a. The graduate committee in the department (or the department’s council in the absence of the
department’s graduate committee) shall approve the thesis examining committee and assign the member with the highest rank and most experienced as a head of the committee whereas the student’s supervisor should be a non-voting member in the committee.
b. The student will introduce a summary of the thesis for 15-20 minutes.
c. The chairman will give the floor to the committee members to examine the student.
d. The committee will withdraw to take its decision privately.
e. The committee will make one of the following decisions:
1. Pass with minor changes
• If the student’s responses to the Committee’s questions during the defense meet the academic criteria for awarding a Master/ Ph.D. degree, but the thesis requires minor changes to meet the required academic standards. • The student is given a period not exceeding three months to make the necessary changes based on the Committee’s report. The student must register zero credit hour for the thesis each semester (if necessary). • The task of ensuring that the student has made all the required changes will be delegated to the supervisor and approved by the examination committee. • If the thesis is not submitted within this time frame, the decision will be converted into No Pass following item 2.i below. If the status stayed the same, the student will be compulsorily withdrawn from the program.
2. No Pass:
If the Committee decides that the thesis, oral defense, or both do not meet the academic criteria for awarding a master’s degree, one of the decisions below will be taken: i. No pass for thesis: the oral defense is satisfactory, but the thesis does not meet the academic criteria for awarding the master’s degree. The student can submit a revised version of the thesis to the defense Committee within a period of a minimum of three to a maximum of six months. The Committee will evaluate the thesis without another oral defense. The thesis evaluation Committee’s report must include a summary of the expected changes.

3.19.16 Comprehension Examination
The student’s study track will be determined at admission time, and it may be changed only once upon a recommendation from the Graduate Committee in the Department and the Dean’s approval.
The comprehensive examination aims to measure the student’s ability to understand the basic principles, demonstrate a general understanding of his discipline, show the ability to create connections between them, and employ them in solving problems and proposing appropriate solutions (the comprehensive examination is not another test in the courses studied by the student).
The student must register for the comprehensive examination only after obtaining the Dean's approval when the student has completed successfully 27 credit hours of the study plan including the remedial courses, the research methodology, and any other conditions stipulated for admission and with a minimum CGPA of 3 out of 4.
The comprehensive examination will be held in the third month of the Fall and Spring semesters only. The examination cannot be conducted twice in one semester. For the purposes of registration, the student shall register for zero credits and a result of fail or pass shall be recorded for him. The Graduate Committees in the Departments may also include an oral test component. The Dean, however, may approve the comprehensive examination to be held in the summer semester upon a recommendation from the Department.
The student may sit for the comprehensive examination twice only. Should he/she fails the second time, he/she will be expelled from the program and may apply to obtain a postgraduate diploma if the program is available in the College.
The Graduate Committee in the Department shall be responsible for organizing the comprehensive
examination by:
1. Determining the major topics of the comprehensive examination and announcing them to the
students (topics are different from courses).
2. Forming committees from Department faculty to write the questions and grade papers in a
confidential manner.
3. Preparing the comprehensive examination in two documents to be given on two separate days.
Each exam shall be a minimum of 3 hours long.
4. Evaluating the results of the comprehensive examination and recording a grade of pass or
fail in special forms.
99
The Dean shall approve the results of the comprehensive examination upon the recommendation of the Graduate Committee in the Department.

3.19.17  Awarding the Postgraduate Diploma
The student shall be awarded the diploma degree, if the program is available in the College, by a
decision of the Council of Deans and the Council of Graduate Studies and upon a proposal from the Department in the following cases:
a. If the student received two “no- pass” in the thesis defense.
If the student fails the comprehensive examination (for the non-thesis track) twice.
b. If the student exceeds the time limit set for the program and completes the required credit hours
with a CGPA of 3 out of 4.
c. If the Graduate Studies Committee in the Department submits a report stating that the student is
unable to complete the thesis after one year from the proposal approval.
d. If the student submits to the Department a written letter to the effect that he/she is unable to
complete the thesis, after approval of the thesis proposal and exceeds the maximum time limit of
the study, and he/she wishes to be awarded the postgraduate diploma.
3.19.18 Committees and their Duties
The Department shall set up at the beginning of each new academic year a graduate studies committee comprising of 3-5 members. It will be headed by the chairman or whoever he/she deputizes provided that academic rank, specialization, and experience are observed in the selection process.
The College Council shall set up at the beginning of each new academic year a graduate studies committee comprising the chairpersons of the graduate studies committees in the relevant Departments plus two senior experienced faculty members in the College if needed. It will be headed by the College Dean or whomever he/she deputizes.
The Graduate Studies Committee in the Department shall have the following duties:
a. Reviewing the Master's application forms and making recommendations to the Dean.
b. Organizing and supervising the comprehensive examination and reporting results to the Dean.
c. Studying the Master's thesis proposals, supervising their oral discussion of the proposals, and
making recommendations to the Dean.
d. Proposing names of defense committees, suggesting dates of defense and reporting the results
to the Dean.
e. Making recommendations to the Dean regarding matters pertaining to postponement,
extension, transfer and equivalence of courses.
100
f. Any other matters the Department council authorizes the committee to act upon or matters
provided for in the rules, regulations, and by-laws.
The Graduate Studies Committee in the College shall have the following powers:
a. Coordinating between College Departments in matters related to graduate studies.
b. Approving new programs of the College.

3.20 Development of New Programs
Academic programs are the core element of the education process. Initiation and development of new potential academic programs is considered as one of the main priorities in the UoS to cover the community and development plan needs.  UoS process of program development is designed based on UoS vision and context as well as the CAA requirements and Standards. This policy outlines the steps and phases for developing new program at UoS.
The main purposes of development new program policy are to:
- Provide a framework for development new academic programs. - Make sure that the academic program offered by UoS is aligned with local and global trends. - Ensure the sustainability of the programs offered by UoS. - Ensure the program developed by UoS are in compliance with, UoS mission and vision, UoS strategic plan and CAA standards. - Give faculty and staff a clear process and procedures for initiating new academic program and engage them in the process. - Attract more students by offering up to date academic programs.
Policy
1- The new programs are developed in alignment with UoS goals, ministry of education vision and UAE national agenda for education system. 2- New proposed program should comply with CAA standard and Ministry of Education requirements. 3- Benchmarking the program with local and International program is considered as very important step before applying for accreditation. 4- The proposal should include details of proper budget to ensure program sustainability. 5- Proposal for new program should take approval from College Council, Deans’ Council and Board of Trustees in sequence before applying to CAA. 6- Preparing the business plan, proposal and initial application documents should be under supervision of The Vice Chancellor office for Institutional Effectiveness and Accreditation

Phase 1: Initiating New Academic Program Idea
- Faculty and staff can investigate for academic opportunities and generate new ideas. - Submit the new idea with evidence and references to the head of department. - Head of department discuss the idea with other faculty member and colleagues. - Head of department prepare a proposal document for new program and discuss it with Vic Chancellor for IEA  and Vice Chancellor for academic affairs.
Phase 2: Preparing Business Plan and Proposal
- Head of Department requests for UoS business plan template from VCIEA. - Head of Department submits complete business plan to the VCIEA for review. - Head of Department shows completed plan to the college council for primary approval.
Phase 3: Application Approval and Confirmation
- After the approval from college council the Dean of the college take the confirmation from Chancellor and Vice Chancellor for academic affairs for presenting new proposed program to the Deans’ Council to take approval. - After approval from Dean’s Council, the Chancellor lists the new proposed program to the BOT Agenda for discuss and takes approval for it. - After Approval from BOT, the college, department offer the program and VCIEA preparing initial application document and appendices based on CAA standards and requirements.
Phase 4: VCIEA Review and Confirmation
- VCIEA keeps review and evaluate the content and format of the application until the application be ready for submitting to CAA. - The Application should be completed based on CAA standards 2019. - VCIEA makes the final approval to submit the application for CAA and make sure the college and department ready for External Review Team (ERT) evaluation process.

- Initial Application is reviewed and evaluated by CAA. - CAA decides to make site visit to evaluate the new proposed program. - VCIEA, Department offer the program and college prepare for the visit and site evaluation process. - CAA gives the feedback and evaluation report to UoS for completing any missing data or requirements. - UoS response to CAA report by compliance and apply all requirements and suggestions. - CAA gives approval and decision letter after ensure that all requirements and standards are applied from a new academic program.

Policy

The chairperson may grant access to others by sending a request for VCIEA. 4- The program E-file for each cycle should have at least; evaluation of program learning outcome, student success rate, student retention rate, enrollment of student,  student graduation rate, Transfer student data, GPA and grade distribution data, survey results from student and faculty related to each program, Alumni employment data. 5- All Programs in UoS are reviewed by external review team and apply for re-accreditation every 3-5 years to keep the program in an active mode and ensure the quality of education delivered to students. 6- All Programs at UoS should have at least a scorecard or key performance indicators to measure the effectiveness of these programs. 7- All these data and assessment should be archived for closing the loop concept and improving the quality of academic program continuously. 8- The Self-Study offers a summary and analysis of the results of program effectiveness, including a discussion of the evaluation instruments used and an indication of changes that have occurred in the program as a result of these measures. The analysis of program effectiveness will include an analysis of the employability of graduates 9- The results from the assessment process are considered as an input for new assessment cycle and continuous improvement process for each program.

3.22 Remedial Courses
Academic knowledge and background is crucial part in the education process.  The UoS offers remedial courses to develop students’ background in such a field and major which may help student entering the program smoothly.  Moreover, the remedial courses will help student apply to the higher level of education with solid educational foundation without any challenges or problems. The remedial course not offers toward a degree or to be in the study plan structure. It is (zero) credit hour and the grade not affects the GPA of the students.
The aim of remedial courses policy is to:
- Make sure that the enrolled students have the minimum requirement of admission before register in the academic program offered by UoS. - Assure that the students have enough knowledge and background before entering the UoS colleges and programs. - Allow students from different field and sector to join their desired programs. - Ensure the program offered by UoS compliance with CAA standards and requirement. - Serve student completing the program study plan without any obstacles. - Show the important of remedial course before taken any such specialized program. - Clarify the correct procedures and condition for registration remedial course.
105
Policy
1- Remedial course may be offered for graduate or undergraduate students. 2- Remedial courses should have a clear course syllabus which contain of a measurable student course learning outcomes (CLOs). 3- Faculty teaching remedial course should have an experience in a field related to the subject and appropriate qualification in related field. 4- Students who are admitted conditionally and required to complete some remedial courses in UOS in order to fulfil the admission requirements, shall register the remedial courses that are specified by UoS. 5- The Student should pass the minimum grade assigned for this course. The student GPA will not include the grade of remedial course. 6- The maximum period to pass the remedial course(s) is specified to the student before register the remedial course. 7- In case students do not pass the remedial course in their first attempt, they have the chance to repeat it the following semester if UoS and ministry of education by-laws allow that. 8- In case the student fails, his/her record may be terminated and leave the institution based on the UoS by-laws and CAA standard. 9- The graduate students can register for credit-bearing course after they have successfully completed remedial course if required. 10- Remediation usually takes place during the first Year (Foundation Year) and it is preferable to be in the first semester to make the program study plan for the student more effective and practical. 11- Each remedial course has E-file for archiving and assessment purposes.

Procedure Remedial Courses for Undergraduate Program - The minimum passing grade for remedial courses is (D). - Remedial courses are non-credit short-term courses offered to undergraduate applicants according to their individual need and lacking sufficient background in a topic which is important - Remedial courses help high school students to compensate needful in short term without major disturbance of semester and other regular teaching-learning duties. - All students taking remedial courses are given conditional admission and are eligible for full admission relevant to the undergraduate program only on passing the same.
Remedial Courses for Graduate Programs
- Students admitted conditionally are not eligible to register in graduate courses unless they complete the prerequisite courses, including remedial courses. - The minimum passing grade in the remedial courses is ‘C’. - Students who are admitted in programs that are taught in Arabic and do not require an English proficiency test; are required to take and pass an English course as a prerequisite during the first semester of enrolment. The student, however, will be exempted from this prerequisite if he/she scores 400 points in TOEFL or 4.0 in the IELTS or any equivalent score in an accepted English proficiency test. - The grades obtained in the remedial courses are not included in the graduate CGPA.
106
- The maximum period to pass the remedial course(s) is communicated to the student before registering the remedial course(s). - Student must finish remedial courses within two semesters. - In case students do not pass the remedial course in their first attempt, they have the chance to repeat it the following semester if UoS and ministry of education by-laws allow that. - In case the student fails, his/her record may be terminated and leave the institution based on the UoS by-laws and CAA standard. - The graduate students can register for credit-bearing course after they have successfully completed remedial course if required. - Each remedial course has E-file for archiving and assessment purposes.
Remedial Courses in College of Engineering and College of Science (Undergraduates)
- Admitted students in the college of engineering and college of science are required to sit for math and physics placement tests to be able to register for freshman-level courses. - Students who do not pass the placements test will be registered in the Math/Physics remedial courses. - Students who do not sit for the placements test will be registered directly in the math/physics remedial courses. - Students who pass the placement tests or the remedial courses are eligible to register in the math and physics (college requirement courses). - Students register for the tests online through a link published on the website. - Students admitted in the qualifying program are registered by registration department.

- Students who hold a General Stream High School certificate and are admitted in the following majors shall be registered in the ‘Qualifying Program’:

Procedure Remedial Courses for Undergraduate Program - The minimum passing grade for remedial courses is (D). - Remedial courses are non-credit short-term courses offered to undergraduate applicants according to their individual need and lacking sufficient background in a topic which is important - Remedial courses help high school students to compensate needful in short term without major disturbance of semester and other regular teaching-learning duties. - All students taking remedial courses are given conditional admission and are eligible for full admission relevant to the undergraduate program only on passing the same.
Remedial Courses for Graduate Programs
- Students admitted conditionally are not eligible to register in graduate courses unless they complete the prerequisite courses, including remedial courses. - The minimum passing grade in the remedial courses is ‘C’. - Students who are admitted in programs that are taught in Arabic and do not require an English proficiency test; are required to take and pass an English course as a prerequisite during the first semester of enrolment. The student, however, will be exempted from this prerequisite if he/she scores 400 points in TOEFL or 4.0 in the IELTS or any equivalent score in an accepted English proficiency test. - The grades obtained in the remedial courses are not included in the graduate CGPA.
106
- The maximum period to pass the remedial course(s) is communicated to the student before registering the remedial course(s). - Student must finish remedial courses within two semesters. - In case students do not pass the remedial course in their first attempt, they have the chance to repeat it the following semester if UoS and ministry of education by-laws allow that. - In case the student fails, his/her record may be terminated and leave the institution based on the UoS by-laws and CAA standard. - The graduate students can register for credit-bearing course after they have successfully completed remedial course if required. - Each remedial course has E-file for archiving and assessment purposes.
Remedial Courses in College of Engineering and College of Science (Undergraduates)
- Admitted students in the college of engineering and college of science are required to sit for math and physics placement tests to be able to register for freshman-level courses. - Students who do not pass the placements test will be registered in the Math/Physics remedial courses. - Students who do not sit for the placements test will be registered directly in the math/physics remedial courses. - Students who pass the placement tests or the remedial courses are eligible to register in the math and physics (college requirement courses). - Students register for the tests online through a link published on the website. - Students admitted in the qualifying program are registered by registration department.

4. Faculty and Professional Staff
4.1 Faculty and Professional Staff Role Policy
Program Coordinator Responsibilities of the program coordinator are:
- Co-operate with the department chairperson/dean for preparing a statement regarding the department’s needs and submitting the program to the Dean at the appropriate time after consultation with the department so that it can be taken into consideration when the budget is prepared. - Help Chairperson/dean for supervising program effectiveness activities to ensure proper documentation of assessment and contentious improvement and development of the program and its courses. - Support chairperson/dean for maintaining records for the activities of the department, records of university documents relating to the department and supervision of their use in accordance with rules and practices followed in the University. - Contribute for selecting of course textbooks and references. - Propose the distribution of courses to be taught among staff members and submit the same to the Chairperson/dean. - Encourage academic research and assisting staff in conducting research. - Help students for preparing suitable study plans and selecting academic advisors for their study period. - Contribute for preparing all reports related to the program which the dean’s office or the university administration requires from the Department. - Coordinate and supervise all assessment activities in the program, including: ▪ Supervise and follow up all the assessment work done in his/her program. ▪ Ensure completion of faculty, course and program e-files according to accreditation
standards and university criteria. ▪ Supervise implementation of recommendations for course and program improvement that
result from the learning outcome assessment process. ▪ Supervise the selection of course textbooks and references. - In case of the program is interdisciplinary, the program coordinator will communicate with all stakeholders to ensure smooth running of the program.
109
Course Coordinator Responsibilities of the course coordinator are:
- Organize and conduct a start-up meeting of all course instructors at the start of each semester. This meeting is about discussing and planning for the implementation of actions developed during the previous cycle.
- Ensure all course instructors follow the course syllabus in order to achieve consistency among all course sections.
- Ensure all course instructors have all course materials and textbooks in advance.
- Coordinate the preparation of unified exams, particularly the midterm and final exams, in cooperation with all course instructors.
- Organize follow up meetings with course instructors during the semester to ensure all sections are progressing similarly.
- Develop and implement course assessment for multi section courses by:
▪ Collecting data, feedback and recommendations related to all sections from all
course instructors, ▪ Compiling aggregate data ▪ Completing the e-course file reflecting the course experience in all sections.

Search and Selection of Faculty - The Vice Chancellor for Academic Affairs ascertains and approves the details of the faculty position
to be filled. - All vacancies, with appropriate details, must be posted at the UoS HR website and other relevant
internationally pre-approved talent acquisition websites along with reasonable advertisement deadline. - The relevant department in consultation with the college dean shall nominate a Hiring Committee
composed of at least three members, preferably professors.  The Hiring Committees at the college level subject to endorsement and approval by the Vice Chancellor for Academic Affairs and shall act as the University agent to search for and attract the best talent for UoS.  All decisions in relation to faculty recruitment are considered in accordance with the principle that all appointments are made solely on merit. All involved members in the search and selection process are expected to observe the highest standards of integrity and objectivity and are consequently expected to adhere to the following principles:
• It is expected that the members of the hiring committees acting on behalf of UoS in a decision-making capacity must not permit any potential conflict of interest to interfere with that obligation which might compromise the integrity of the decision making process. • Are responsible for avoiding potential or actual conflicts of interest. If a situation arises at any time that could present a conflict of interest, a full disclosure of the relevant
111
information must be made to the relevant academic administrator (department chair/dean or the VCAA). • Are requested to declare any personal relationship / previous work relationship (as a manager, subordinate, and colleague) with the candidate. - At the beginning of each year, each college shall form a Department and College Hiring Committees.
The Department Hiring Committee chaired by the department chair or designee and consists of at least three members with the rank of professor or associate professor shall:
• Secure reliable and detailed information on candidates to ensure that a decision is made based on a candidate’s merit; • Write a letter describing in detail the search positions including the job descriptions, qualifications, and deadlines in consultation with the department chair and the dean; • Advertise the position publicly in addition to using other appropriate methods of candidate solicitation (in coordination with UoS HR); • Review the applicants’ pool; • Select and shortlist candidates for interviews and/or campus visits; • Recommend candidates for appointments to the College Hiring Committee. - The College Hiring Committee consists of the Dean or designee as a chair and a representative from
each department with the rank of professor/associate professor.  The College Hiring Committee shall:
• Review the department recommendations. • Endorse or reject the recommendation of the department’s recommendation.  The Committee may interview the candidate if deemed necessary. • Recommend endorsed candidates to the University Central Committee. - The Central hiring committee shall be appointed by the Chancellor at the beginning of each
academic year.  The Central Committee shall review, evaluate, and recommend hiring of new faculty based on the policies and procedures established by the University. The Chancellor has the final approval for all recommended candidates. - The HR, when approved by the Chancellor, shall provide the selected candidate with a detailed offer

leaders, and scholars of international reputation to occupy an endowed chair or a professorship as one of the highest forms of recognition provided by the University. An endowed chair or professorship is intended to improve an existing program by providing support to attract new faculty members. It can also reward an individual of exceptional accomplishments who is already a faculty member at UoS. In addition to rewarding excellence, an endowed position carries with it the expectation of continuing worthy contributions. Many donors stipulate specific requirements for an endowed chair or professorship. This endowment process must be sufficiently flexible to meet the desires and wishes of the donors while adhering to all University policies. - Emeritus Professor: When an individual retires holding the rank of professor, he or she may be
eligible for consideration for the title “Emeritus Professor.” In addition to having served at UoS for a minimum of six years, faculty must have shown excellence in teaching, research, or administration, produced scholarly publication(s) and research, and offered a service of distinction to the University, the community, and professional discipline. Emeritus faculty residents in Sharjah may be accorded office space, secretarial assistance, and access to University services depending on availability. Appointments as Emeritus Professors must be endorsed by the Chancellor and approved by the President. - Other title modifier appointment: A policy specific to the title modifier appointment shall be
applied at the time of employment.
Hiring Exceptions The Chancellor has the jurisdiction to appoint without the regular review and appointment process (1) national faculty who fulfills the required criteria and (2) professors with high Scopus H index or rare specializations.

His/her employment may be renewed for three (3) years once the current contract expires after successful annual evaluations in accordance with UoS policies. Thereafter, his/her contract may be renewed for four (4) years after successful annual evaluation in accordance with the Uos evaluation policies.  The regular faculty member must apply for promotion to associate professor during his appointment and must be within the ten years of obtaining the assistant professor rank.  The 10th year of the contract shall be conditional on obtaining the promotion.  Failure to have a successful promotion on the 10th year will lead an automatic termination of contract. Faculty who applies for promotion on their 8th years and fail promotion shall be given a second chance to apply for promotion.  A second failure shall lead to an automatic termination of contract. Similar condition applies for the associate professor, however, he/she must obtain the promotion within their 12th year of attaining the associate professor rank.

• Joint appointment: When a faculty member is hired to perform ongoing responsibilities across two or more units within UoS, a joint appointment is possible. A joint appointment requires that no less than 60% of that appointment must be held in a home unit, with that unit having responsibility for all decisions regarding annual performance review, promotion, and other conditions associated with that position in accordance with the policies of that unit and the UoS. Individuals holding a joint appointment must meet the qualifications for faculty at the rank in which he or she is appointed. All joint appointments are recommended by Deans of Colleges, and approved by the UoS. Joint faculty members are integrated into the University’s academic scheme, and should be recruited, reviewed, appointed, retained and terminated, as defined for the fulltime faculty. The performance of a joint faculty should be reviewed by the dean or appropriate supervisor of primary unit annually to ensure that his/her contributions continue to meet the expectations of the unit. Joint faculty members should be included on all correspondence or communications of both units and are eligible to sit on the committees of both units.
• Adjunct/Parttime appointment: Adjunct/Parttime faculty members are appointed to colleges with approval of the respective dean after being reviewed by the appropriate College Committee. The faculty member must be from outside UoS, and, for an individual to be appointed as an adjunct/parttime faculty, he/she must offer substantial contributions to the teaching and/or research objectives of a college. The rank for which an adjunct member is being considered must be determined by applying the same criteria and evaluated on evidence presented to appropriate committees and deans as those for faculty appointed within UoS. The performance of an adjunct/parttime faculty should be reviewed at the conclusion of each semester to ensure that his/her contributions continue to meet the expectations of the college in which he/she has been appointed. The dean is responsible for informing an adjunct faculty member about the mission and objectives of the college.

Appointments may be recommended to cover short-term faculty vacancies, including those caused by retirements, leaves of absence, or temporary increase in teaching load. Visiting Faculty appointment must have a formal teaching responsibilities and shall make identifiable contributions to the college through research and service.  Appointment as Visiting Associate Professor or Visiting Professor will require evidence of professional achievements equivalent to those of faculty of the same rank at the department and or college. - The faculty contracts may be terminated by the UoS in the event that academic
colleges/divisions/departments are discontinued and faculty cannot be transferred to other departments for any reason or in the event that the BOT has declared a financial emergency which requires reduction of faculty consistent with the needs of the University, the availability of funded positions and in accordance with UoS HR Policies.  Terminated faculty shall be provided with a minimum of a six-month notice. - The faculty contracts may be recommended for cause. The final decision on the termination of a
faculty shall require the approval of the Chancellor.
Probation and Resignation Notice - The faculty probation period shall be one year months.  Under exceptional circumstances, and with
the approval of the Chancellor, the probation period may be, under no circumstance the probation period maybe extended beyond two years.  A termination of the contract during the probation period may be recommended by the dean and or the vice chancellors and or the chancellor. Recommendation for terminating the contract of a faculty member during probation must be for cause. The final decision on the termination of the contract of a faculty shall require the collective approval of the Dean, the Vice Chancellor and the Chancellor.  Termination the contract of a faculty during the probation period entitles the affected faculty with a six-month notice. Faculty intending to resign during the probation period shall provide UoS with a six-month notice. - A faculty member who intend to resign from UoS shall submit his/her resignation at least six months
prior to the date it takes effect.  Normally the effective date of a resignation shall coincide with the end of a regular semester.  If a faculty insists on resigning without adhering to the minimum six- month notice, the faculty’s end of service compensation may be subjected to a 50% deduction. Exceptions may be granted by the Chancellor. - New faculty who are terminated by UoS during the probation period will be entitled to return tickets
to their home (unless they decide to remain in the UAE, while new faculty member who resign during the probation period will not be entitled).

- New faculty will not be eligible for benefits such as annual leave and tickets allowance during the
probation period, they will, however, be eligible for medical insurance coverage, compassionate leave, and authorized sick leave subject to submission of appropriate documentation and obtaining relevant approvals.

• Not to renew contract • Extend probation for one more year. • Renew contract for one to two years (Teaching) • Renew contract for one to three years (Teaching and Research). - New faculty members must be notified in writing of their employment confirmation or termination

• Submission of evidence of all employment requirements with authentic documents which may include proof of educational, professional qualification and certificates etc. • Submission of education attestation and equivalency evidence and approvals • Eligibility to work in the UAE, i.e. residency visa or eligibility for sponsorship • Completion of pre-employment medical check-up • Completion of background check/references • Obtaining the Security Clearance • Obtaining the Good Conduct Certificate – for applicants from within the UAE • Not being previously convicted of crimes related to integrity and honor / or being convicted but the conviction was revoked • Not being previously terminated with a court order / final disciplinary decision • Satisfactory previous employment history
- HR will be responsible for managing all communication with candidates and potential recruits from
post selection phase to the joining and induction phase. This is to ensure the following:
• Communicating UoS’s brand and prompting its image as an Employer of Choice • Stimulating positive candidate experience and building potential employees’ engagement • Implementing effective communication through delivering unified, standard and consistent messages while addressing candidate’s special requirements • Delivering comprehensive, clear and accurate information to candidates as per the approved policies and guidelines • Steering the employment  process to enhance effectiveness and efficiency as well as enable monitoring and improvement.

Clearance. Typically, employment offers will only be made after the approval of the Security Clearance request. The VCAA Office Shall communicate with the HR further direction for acquiring a candidate for the position.

118
Scale. HR is responsible for ensuring that all relevant details and employment terms are outlined in the Employment Offer to enable the candidate to make informed decisions. Pre-joining Formalities - Employee Records
• HR will be responsible for compiling all the documents, authentications and information required to be maintained in the Employee File as per the approved polices and statutory requirements. • New faculty members must be informed of their responsibility to promptly notify Talent Acquisition of any changes in personal data and documents. • Employee records are the property of UoS, and access to the information contained in the file must highly restricted. Only designated HR personnel, approved internal and external audit personnel are allowed access.
- Document Authentication
• Authenticated documents are required as a condition of employment with the UoS as they are necessary for obtaining residence visas in the UAE and for the employee’s eligibility for family status. • HR shall inform the new faculty members of the documents which should be attested in the home country prior to relocation to UAE (e.g. Family Records Book, Marriage Contract, Children’s Birth Certificates, Dependent(s)' School Reports), and that further authenticating will be required upon arrival in the UAE. • HR is responsible for insuring and facilitating the process of delivering clear, comprehensive and accurate information to new faculty members at all times. An Employee Handbook should be developed and shared with the new joiners after accepting the Employment Offer. The Employee Handbook may include the following information:
o Overview of UoS. o History. o Leadership and Governance. o Organization Structure. o Senior Management. o Strategic Plan / Objectives. o Vision and Mission Statements. o Core Values. o Role of HR. o HR Policies. o Employment Policies. o Working Hours. o Code of Conduct. o Dress Code. o Performance Management.
119
o Training & Development. o New Joiners’ Information.
• Information about Living in the UAE (Sharjah)
o Local Culture and Customs. o Immigration Requirements. o Relocation Services (Shipping, Courier). o Housing, Schools, Hospitals, Banks. o Transport, Telecommunication. o Settling in the UAE.
• HR shall inform new joiners that all queries should be directed to HR by email and will be attended to promptly. HR shall liaise with the internal concerned stakeholders to obtain the required information and share with the new joiners.
- Entry Visas to the UAE
• HR must inform new faculty member of the legal requirements and request the required documents to obtain an entry visa through the Passport Unit. • HR shall inform the new faculty member once the visa is issued.
- Travel and Hotel Arrangements
• HR shall make the necessary travel and hotel arrangement in coordination with the new faculty member after obtaining the entry visa. • New faculty will be allowed hotel stay for the duration of 5 days – to be extended if required. • Talent Acquisition will make the necessary travel arrangements for the new faculty’s dependents upon the issue of the new faculty’s residency visa.
- Joining Arrangements
• Talent Acquisition will inform the concerned internal parties to ensure the availability of the required facilities/tools upon joining (e.g.):
o Work space / stationary. o Email Account. o Other Resources / Tools.

Joining Formalities - Joining Date / Confirmation
• The joining date will be determined as per the academic calendar. • HR may cancel the Employment Offer if the employee does not join on the specified date, unless a prior approval has been obtained. • New faculty will be advised to report to HR on the joining date. HR will be responsible for receiving new faculty member and carrying out the joining formalities. • New faculty will be accompanied by HR to their respective departments to meet with their department chairs and or deans.
- Employees Files
• HR is responsible for reviewing the new faculty’s file to ensure its inclusiveness of all required documents as well as the addition of all employment related documentations. • HR must ensure that new faculty member submit all the required information - if not previously provided - upon joining.
120
• The Employee Information System will be updated to reflect the new faculty’s data and joining date.
- Confidentiality Agreement / Conflict of Interest Declaration
• New faculty will be requested to sign a ‘Confidentiality Agreement’ and ‘Conflict of Interest Declaration’ upon joining UoS. • New faculty are required to declare any form of conflict of interest at the time of joining UoS, or immediately upon a conflict arises, due to any change in circumstances during the course of their employment.

• HR shall provide new faculty member with an Employee ID Card in a prescribed format upon joining.  The Card is intended to serve as an identification of the employment status with UoS. • Staff are required to carry the Employee ID Card at all times during working hours. • The Employee ID Card is not transferable and any misuse of the same will lead to disciplinary actions. • Loss of the Employee ID Card should be directly reported in writing to Talent Acquisition. • The Employee ID Card remains the property of UoS and must be returned to Employee Engagement upon exiting UoS.
- Bank Accounts
• A new faculty is  required to provide details of bank account for the transfer the monthly salary and other dues. • HR shall provide the required information and assistance to new faculty member from outside the UAE to facilitate the process.

• HR shall arrange for the new faculty member to enroll under the UoS Medical Plan to avail the provided coverage and obtain the Insurance Card. • HR shall ensure that the new faculty member is fully informed on the provided benefits and services, health providers and claim procedures. • The new faculty’s dependents will be enrolled under the Plan – as per the employee’s entitlement – upon arriving in the UAE.

• New employee announcements allow the new faculty member to feel welcomed and inform other employees of new faculty’s arrival. • Upon the completion of the joining formalities and directing the new faculty member to the concerned department, Talent Acquisition will draft and publish the announcement email which should reflect the following:
o Name. o College. o Line Manager. o Role / Key Responsibilities. o Academic Background. o Professional Background. o Professional / Personal Achievements. o Optional: Personal Facts (Family, Hobbies, Interests) – to be provided. by
the new faculty member.

4.3 Employment Policy
Employees are appointed as per the following contracts:
4.3.1 Temporary Contracts
Where the employee is contracted to do a job that is not continuous and requires a limited time to be done. Here the employee's appointment ends by the end of the job.
Rights of Contracted Employees
- Employees with temporary contracts are not entitled to tickets or medical insurance. Instead, they are given a lump sum including all allowances and advantages. This lump sum is determined by the Committee and approved by the Chancellor, depending on the nature of work and qualifications required to be satisfied by the employee. - Employees with permeant contracts are given tickets and children education allowances, medical insurance according to their respective grades. - Employees' salaries, whether hired by permanent or temporary contracts, are paid via a Personal Action Form done by the Human Resources Department and approved by the Vice-Chancellor and the Director of Human Resources Department, and then forwarded to the Financial Department for payment. - In case the employee starts his/her work after the beginning of the month, or ends his/her services before the end of the month, the salary will be calculated by the proportion of days of work
123
(including official holidays and week-ends that come within normal working days) to the total number of days in that particular month. - The employees' salaries will be transferred to their bank accounts via the bank which the University is dealing with, whenever this is possible. - The Human Resources Department will enter, and modify, the employee's personal data like their monthly salaries, allowances, and advantages. - The employee will be notified of the details of his/her monthly salary, along with deductions, if any. - The employee should present an annual statement indicating any change to their social status. In the event of presenting incorrect data, the employee will be suspended and referred to interrogation.
4.3.2 Raises and Allowances - In-Kind Advantages
The employee is entitled to the regular raise specified for his/her grade as per the table enclosed with these by-laws. This raise, however, is due only after the passage of one year on the employee's appointment, subject to a decision issued by the Chancellor, or whomever he may deputize, upon recommendation from the Committee.

title: Policies and Procedures Manual
text:
4.3.2 Raises and Allowances - In-Kind Advantages
The employee is entitled to the regular raise specified for his/her grade as per the table enclosed with these by-laws. This raise, however, is due only after the passage of one year on the employee's appointment, subject to a decision issued by the Chancellor, or whomever he may deputize, upon recommendation from the Committee.
The employee who is reported to have Excellent Performance may be given additional, incentive raise/bonus within the category of his/her regular raise and grade. An employee, however, shall not have more than one bonus in two years, as per the following rules:
- An employee shall not have this incentive raise more than once per annum. - This incentive raise is paid to the employee by the date of its approval by the Chancellor, upon the Committee's recommendations. - Incentive raise is paid in each department with an average not more than 10% of employees receiving this raise.
The Human Resources Department will prepare lists with the names of employees deserving the regular or incentive raises and put them before the Committee prior to the due time.
Some employees with specialized qualifications may be granted an allowance called (Rareness Allowance) equal to 20 % of the basic salary. This is done by a decision from the Chancellor, upon recommendation from the Director of competent department and the Committee as well.
4.3.3 Education Allowance
- The University will undertake the education fees for the non-National employee's children enrolled in preliminary to general secondary stages inside the State. The University will pay a maximum of AED 6000 (six thousand Dirhams) for the only child, and a maximum of 12000 (twelve thousand Dirhams) for two children in accordance with the regulations of the country's competent authorities in this regard. - Employees appointed or promoted before 1/1/2008 at the grades 1 – 3 shall receive a maximum of AED 20,000 for the only child, and a maximum of AED 40,000 for all the children. - Those fees and expenses are paid according to original receipts or invoices. - Each of the employees, nationals and non-nationals, is also entitled to two scholarships for two of his/her children for studying at the University of Sharjah.
4.3.4 Travel Tickets
Employees are entitled to get Air tickets when they go on their regular vacations. This will be as follows:
First: For non-national employees
- Grades 1-3: Air ticket allowance every year for the employee, his wife, and three of his children who are less than 18 years of age
124
- Grades 4-9: one ticket for the employee himself every year. - Grades 10-12: one ticket for the employee himself every other year.
Second: For UAE and GCC national employees:

4.3.2 Raises and Allowances - In-Kind Advantages
The employee is entitled to the regular raise specified for his/her grade as per the table enclosed with these by-laws. This raise, however, is due only after the passage of one year on the employee's appointment, subject to a decision issued by the Chancellor, or whomever he may deputize, upon recommendation from the Committee.
The employee who is reported to have Excellent Performance may be given additional, incentive raise/bonus within the category of his/her regular raise and grade. An employee, however, shall not have more than one bonus in two years, as per the following rules:
- An employee shall not have this incentive raise more than once per annum. - This incentive raise is paid to the employee by the date of its approval by the Chancellor, upon the Committee's recommendations. - Incentive raise is paid in each department with an average not more than 10% of employees receiving this raise.
The Human Resources Department will prepare lists with the names of employees deserving the regular or incentive raises and put them before the Committee prior to the due time.
Some employees with specialized qualifications may be granted an allowance called (Rareness Allowance) equal to 20 % of the basic salary. This is done by a decision from the Chancellor, upon recommendation from the Director of competent department and the Committee as well.
4.3.3 Education Allowance
- The University will undertake the education fees for the non-National employee's children enrolled in preliminary to general secondary stages inside the State. The University will pay a maximum of AED 6000 (six thousand Dirhams) for the only child, and a maximum of 12000 (twelve thousand Dirhams) for two children in accordance with the regulations of the country's competent authorities in this regard. - Employees appointed or promoted before 1/1/2008 at the grades 1 – 3 shall receive a maximum of AED 20,000 for the only child, and a maximum of AED 40,000 for all the children. - Those fees and expenses are paid according to original receipts or invoices. - Each of the employees, nationals and non-nationals, is also entitled to two scholarships for two of his/her children for studying at the University of Sharjah.

4.4.2 Academic Promotion
Promotion to the Rank of Associate Professor: An assistant professor applying for promotion to the rank of associate professor shall:
A. Have spent a minimum of five years as an assistant professor, of which at least one year
has been at the University of Sharjah.
B. Submit a minimum of six original publications in his/her field of specialization, or a closely
related field, of which at least three must be journal articles where the applicant is solo or main author. In the case of joint authorship, applicants are required to specify their contribution for each publication and verify this by the main author. The main author is determined taking into consideration the practice of the journals in the different categories (disciplines) and his field of specialization.
C. Have had at least three actually published articles.
D. Have had research articles accepted for publication or published while in the rank of
assistant professor that have not been used to fulfill earlier academic degree requirements (i.e. Master’s or PhD degrees). A maximum of two journal papers published after obtaining Ph. D. and outside the period of Assistant Professor may be considered.
E. Have had at least two journal articles published (or accepted for publication) while
working at the University of Sharjah.

two journal articles published or accepted for publication in a class (A) journal in which the applicant must be solo or main author.

Applications for promotion shall be processed at the University level as follows: A. The committee may ask the applicant for additional information and supporting documentation pertaining to the contents of his/her promotion dossier. C. The Chancellor or his deputy shall select four referees from the referees nominated by the college or others specialized in the field to evaluate whether or not an applicant’s research complies with the promotion criteria. The Chancellor or his deputy may add the names of other specialized referees after consulting with the members of the Central Promotions Committee. The Chancellor or his deputy shall be in charge of corresponding with the referees. D. Each referee shall be sent a copy of the applicant's CV, the University’s promotion by-laws, the research accepted for promotion by the Central Promotions Committee, and a designated questionnaire for evaluating the applicant’s research. The Chancellor or his deputy may send the dossier to a replacement referee if any of the original referees do not respond within a period of three months. E. The minimum overall average of the three referees evaluating the research of an applicant for promotion to the rank of associate professor must be at least 75 %. 2. 4.4.9 Policy on Misconduct in research
Professional integrity is of core importance at all reputable educational institutions including research institutions and universities. The University of Sharjah is responsible for providing a suitable environment that fosters intellectual and professional integrity and honesty and therefore does not tolerate misconduct in any aspect of research or scholarly endeavor.
133
The University’s policy is based upon the following professional and ethical standards that have been well established in the field of research: • Applying scholarly and scientific rigor and integrity in obtaining, recording and analyzing data and in reporting and publishing results (not fabricating or falsifying data or results). • Recognizing the substantive contributions of all collaborators (e.g. using the unpublished work of other researchers and scholars only upon their consent and providing them due acknowledgment). • Ensuring that the authorship of published work includes all persons who have materially contributed to and/or share responsibility for the contents of the publication, and only those persons. • Obtaining written consent from authors before using new information, concepts or data originally obtained through access to confidential manuscripts or applications or through refereeing or participating in refereeing projects submitted by other researchers with the aim of securing project funding. • Obtaining approval from the Research Ethics Committee before engaging in any research that involves human and animal subjects and complying fully with the approved research protocol in performing such research. • Stating in writing to research sponsors (whether this university or another), journals or funding agencies, any material conflict of interest (financial and/or other) that might influence a sponsor’s decision or a sponsor’s request of an individual to review research or research project funding applications, test products or to undertake work sponsored by external sources.
Misconduct in research is not limited to any deviation from the above stated standards. It is the University’s responsibility to investigate all allegations of misconduct in research involving any researchers at the University and to take any appropriate action necessary in a prompt and effective manner. For more details on the University’s research code of conduct, faculty members may refer to the University’s detailed policy on this matter.
4.4.10 Appeals
1. If an application for promotion of faculty member is denied he/she may submit an appeal in writing to the chancellor. The appeals must be made in writing within one week of notification of the results of the promotion process and results. Appeals should address the specific procedural grounds upon which the request is based. 2. The Chancellor will form a committee to look into the case. The committee will make recommendations to the Chancellor within three weeks. The Chancellor may uphold or overturn the original decision based on the committee recommendations. The decision of the Chancellor is final and is communicated to the Dean and the concerned faculty member. Should the application for promotion be approved, the HR Department is notified. 3. Once a final decision has been reached, all original documents prepared and submitted by the candidate will be returned to the faculty promotion office. All confidential reports are withheld in the Chancellor’s Office.

Seminal activities to the mission of the University are teaching or librarianship; research, scholarship and artistry, creative activity, academic advising; administrative and community service. 2. Private Professional Work, Consulting, and Outside Employment Private professional work, consulting, outside employment, and other bases of supplemental compensation should not be a factor in workload assessment and determination in any University workload assignments, requests for adjustments, and/or requests for other teaching assignments. Workload adjustments and/or other teaching assignments should not be requested, assigned, and/or approved for any extra-compensation activities.
Variations to Normal Workload Assignments To effectively fulfill the University’s responsibilities and achieve its mission, it is sometimes prudent to adjust individual faculty members’ workloads. Such adjustments may include replacing one or more teaching assignments with other workload assignments. Such assignments might include administrative duties, unusually heavy academic support or university service roles, extraordinary research/scholarly/creative activity. Adjustments to an individual faculty members’ normal workload for the type of faculty appointment may be made by the University Chancellor, Vice Chancellors, or the faculty member’s academic dean. Adjustments proposed by the department head must be approved by the dean and Vice Chancellor.
Determining Workload Credits Typically, each assigned teaching workload credit is equivalent to each course credit hour taught (e.g., each 3 credit-hour-course taught would be equivalent to 3 workload credits). However, variations exist for different types of courses (e.g., student contact hours are considered in determining the workload credit for natural science laboratory classes; workload credit for applied music classes are determined by a formula that takes into consideration enrollment and course credit hours). Exceptions to using course credit hours for determining teaching workload credits must be approved by the dean of the course and Vice Chancellor. Non-instructional workload assignments are typically made in 3-credit increments. The workload credits associated with non-instructional assignments are based on an estimate of the amount of work involved and its equivalent to teaching one or more 3-credit courses.
Overloads Overloads should be avoided and are justified only by extenuating circumstances such as a sudden resignation or illness of a faculty member and/or an unexpected enrollment demand. Generally, faculty are in overload status when their total assigned workload exceeds their official maximum workload. An overload assignment of more than 1 credit/contact hour must be approved by the dean and the Vice Chancellor. Overloads are compensated in accordance with the University’s
138
current overload pay scale. Typically, faculty members receiving course release(s) for a service assignment or an additional research assignment do not receive teaching overload compensation.

4.7 Eligibility to Teach Graduate Courses and Supervise Theses
4.7.1 Criteria for Selection of Faculty to Participate in Graduate Programs
a) In order to participate in the teaching of graduate courses, serving on graduate
thesis/dissertation committees, or serving as major advisor to a student at the master’s or doctoral level, faculty must be qualified to serve by the Graduate Studies Council. These faculty members are selected from the University faculty on the basis of academic training, experience, demonstrated potential for creative work and scholarly research, and evidence of the ability and competency essential to directing and supervising graduate students in their pursuit of advanced knowledge. b) Faculty members are nominated by the Department chairperson and the dean of that college.
Final review and approval is given by the Graduate Studies Council.
4.7.2 Teach graduate courses
Evidence of effective instruction or effectiveness in other types of professional presentations should be supplied. Strong record of active engagement in research and scholarship related to the discipline is expected. Minimum academic rank: Assistant Professor (except for professional programs in which case a faculty is required to have significant professional experience as a practitioner in the discipline).
4.7.3 Direct non-thesis students
Evidence of professional activity or scholarship sufficient to assure awareness of current advances in the discipline or profession. Evidence of effectiveness in advising and directing non-thesis student programs should be supplied for re-designations. Minimum academic rank: Assistant Professor (except for professional programs in which case a faculty is required to have significant professional experience as a practitioner in the discipline).
4.7.4 Serve on graduate student committees
Doctorate degree appropriate to the student's degree level. Evidence of professional activity or scholarship sufficient to assure awareness of current advances in the discipline or profession. Evidence of effectiveness in advising, participation on graduate student committees, and supervising graduate student research should be supplied for re-designations. Minimum academic rank: Assistant Professor (except in the case of external co-advisor/committee
144
member who should have a doctoral degree and whose qualifications will be approved by the Dean of the College of Graduate Studies).
4.7.5 Supervise master's theses
Doctorate degree in a relevant field. Evidence of professional activity in the discipline or profession. Strong record of active engagement in research and scholarship related to the discipline is expected. Evidence of experience and effectiveness of service on graduate student committees is preferred. Evidence of successful participation in the advising of graduate students and the directing of master's thesis research should be supplied for re-designations. Minimum academic rank: Assistant Professor.
4.7.6 Supervise doctoral dissertations
Doctorate degree in a relevant field. Evidence of professional activity in the discipline or profession. Strong record of active engagement in research and scholarship related to the discipline is required. Evidence of successful participation in directing of master students’ research and service on doctoral dissertation committees is required. Evidence of successful participation in the advising of graduate students and the directing of doctoral thesis research should be supplied for re-designations. Minimum academic rank: Assistant Professor and a minimum of one of the other advisory committee members holding a rank of Associate Professor or higher; except in the case of an external committee member who will normally have a doctoral degree and whose qualifications will be approved by the Dean of the College of Graduate Studies.

Strong record of active engagement in research and scholarship related to the discipline is expected. Evidence of experience and effectiveness of service on graduate student committees is preferred. Evidence of successful participation in the advising of graduate students and the directing of master's thesis research should be supplied for re-designations. Minimum academic rank: Assistant Professor.
4.7.6 Supervise doctoral dissertations
Doctorate degree in a relevant field. Evidence of professional activity in the discipline or profession. Strong record of active engagement in research and scholarship related to the discipline is required. Evidence of successful participation in directing of master students’ research and service on doctoral dissertation committees is required. Evidence of successful participation in the advising of graduate students and the directing of doctoral thesis research should be supplied for re-designations. Minimum academic rank: Assistant Professor and a minimum of one of the other advisory committee members holding a rank of Associate Professor or higher; except in the case of an external committee member who will normally have a doctoral degree and whose qualifications will be approved by the Dean of the College of Graduate Studies.

4.7.7 Terminal Degree
Faculty teaching courses and supervising theses or dissertations in graduate degree programs should have a terminal degree in the discipline. Exceptions to the requirement for a terminal degree, which must be justified and documented by the college, are: a) Limited to faculty members in applied fields who have a minimum of either:
I. A master’s degree in the teaching field or a doctorate in a related field, and who also have
extensive senior level experience in the applied field (such as corporate management or accounting); II. Experience in the applied field coupled with internationally recognized professional
association certification (such as medical board certificate or Certified Public Accountant). b) Fully justifiable in terms of education, training, and professional experience; c) Restricted to no more than 10% of all faculty in the institution; or d) Are reported to the Commission for Academic Accreditation for approval prior to the start of the
semester in which the faculty member will teach. Reports to the must include the name of the faculty member for whom the exception is requested, the highest degree earned and the conferring institution, the area of specialization, the justification for the exception, and a listing of the courses assigned.
4.8 Compensation Policy
Medical Insurance, Housing, and Education of Children
Faculty members and their families shall be covered by medical insurance in accordance with regulations issued by the Chancellor.
The University shall bear the annual tuition fees including the textbooks of the faculty members’ children with a maximum amount of AED 20,000 for each child and AED 40,000 for all children starting from KG2 till the end of the secondary school stage. Fees shall be paid against official receipts. The University shall also offer two educational grants for two children together at the same time to study at any college of the University of Sharjah except the colleges of Medicine and Dentistry where part
145
of the fees, determined by the University Administration, is born by the concerned faculty member.
The University provides faculty members with appropriate housing at its own cost, and a one-time furniture allowance of AED (30,000) thirty thousand dirhams is given to each faculty member. If the length of service at the University is less than four years, the furniture allowance shall be partially paid back to the University according to a linear depreciation model.
4.9 Faculty Annual Evaluation
4.9.1 General
All faculty members will be evaluated annually in each of the three areas of scholarship (including research and creative activity), teaching, and service. In addition, faculty members will be evaluated on contributions to the quality and effectiveness of their Unit, their College, and the University in the light of UoS mission. The University recognizes that every faculty member offers a unique combination of accomplishments relative to the criteria listed above, depending on academic field, specialized scholarly interests, varying professional opportunities, and responsibilities for teaching, laboratory and field work. However, while relative weights may vary, all faculty members are expected to be productive in each of the three areas over time.
Performance criteria in the areas of scholarship, teaching effectiveness and service shall be delineated in each Unit's documents concerning merit review, reappointment, and promotion policies.

title: Policies and Procedures Manual
text:
